summary: Jon Hyltner, small-cap fund manager at Pareto Småbolagsfond with 10-year experience, discusses his investment philosophy focusing on premium companies with reasonable valuations rather than deep value. He explains lessons learned from the low interest rate period, including avoiding companies like Viaplay that took on excessive growth strategies. Hyltner highlights portfolio holdings like Lagerkranz, Carnov, Avanza and Nordnet as examples of quality companies with sustainable business models, while discussing challenges in the small-cap segment with weak profit growth currently. He expects a turnaround when profits recover, driven by consumption and construction activity.
key_takeaways: Focus on premium companies with strong profitability rather than low multiples alone
Small-cap market currently weak with only 6% average profit growth versus historical 18% five-year average
Acquisition companies like Lagerkranz, Adtech, Lifco have performed well through disciplined M&A strategies
AI represents significant upside potential for Carnov through additional revenue modules
IPO market expected to pick up with better market conditions, but current expectations are often too high
Consumer exposure more difficult to evaluate than industrial businesses with recurring replacement needs
